title: Haemodynamic monitoring to optimize intraoperative perfusion during free flap surgery and detection of systemic inflammatory response
summary:
To cover large wounds involving soft tissue and to restore the body’s shape and function, doctors often use a method called free flap transfer. In this type of surgery, a piece of tissue — including the blood vessels that supply it — is taken from one part of the body and moved to another area where it is needed. The blood vessels are then reconnected at the new site to keep the tissue alive.
However, during these surgeries, patients sometimes experience problems with their circulation or organs. This may be caused by the body’s inflammatory response, which is how the body reacts to stress or injury. This reaction can not only reduce the chances of the surgery being successful but also pose a risk to the patient’s overall health.
The reasons for this strong inflammatory response during surgery are complex and not yet fully understood. It is also unclear how this reaction affects how much fluid (like IV fluids) a patient needs during the operation.
The HEMOptis study is designed to observe and learn more about this. During the surgeries, doctors will closely monitor the patient’s fluid needs and how their heart and circulation are doing, using a special device. This helps keep the body stable and allows the team to measure exactly how much fluid the patient requires. At specific times, blood samples will be taken to check for signs of inflammation and tissue damage.
Only adult patients who are able to give their consent will take part in the study. After the surgeries, the collected data will be analyzed to see how inflammation and tissue damage are related to the patient’s fluid needs.
conditions: The extent of inflammation and endothelial damage on the volume/catecholamine requirements during free flap surgery is being investigated

interventions.name:
The observational cohort includes all patients undergoing free flap surgery who meet the inclusion criteria, no interventional cohort. 
As part of this study, blood parameters will be assessed at the following time points while maintaining normovolemia, as verified by hemodynamic monitoring: preope

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age > 18 years

- Free flap reconstruction from the following specialties: oral and maxillofacial surgery, hand surgery, plastic surgery (the soft tissue defect may be pre-existing or planned as part of a procedure, e.g., tumor resection)

- informed consent given by patients
Exclusion criteria:
- Pregnancy

- Age < 18 years

- Refusal to participate in the study by patients capable of giving informed consent

- previous free flap transfer (FLT) performed at the same anatomical site

- coagulation disorders / ongoing anticoagulant medication

- current immunosuppressive therapy

- atrial fibrillation

- chronic inflammatory diseases (COPD, chronic inflammatory bowel diseases, rheumatoid disease spectrum)
